trial_court: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh, CRM No.M-5130 of 2017
case_name: Surinder Kaur And Ors vs State Of Punjab And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Surinder Kaur and others (wife, husband, etc.)

facts_of_case: Matrimonial discord between respondent No.2 and petitioner No.3 led to FIR under Sections 406/498A/120B IPC. Parties arrived at a compromise, which was recorded by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise in a matrimonial dispute can be quashed if it is arrived at out of the free will and volition of the parties without any coercion, fear or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: The Court has observed that the compromise, in a modern society, is genuine when arrived at out of the free will and volition of the parties without any coercion, fear or undue influence.
cited_cases: Kulwinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2007) 3 R.C.R. (Criminal) 1052

outcome.final_order: FIR No.213 dated 19.09.2015 and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom are quashed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
